query_wording: What implementation bottlenecks does the latest reporting identify, and which actions are assigned to the government or the Bank?

placeholders.reason: The query assumes a project in context; it is named in the turn. Its latest reporting includes a disclosed midterm review aide-memoire with an agreed-actions table.

turns.user: For P164920, what implementation bottlenecks does the latest reporting identify, and which actions are assigned to the government or the Bank?

expected_sources.role: Midterm review aide-memoire: bottlenecks and Table 1 of agreed actions with responsibilities
AF2 paper: later status of the same bottlenecks

text: Latest reporting: the latest ISR (seq. 10, 9 Aug 2026) says only that disbursement is at 43 percent and implementation should accelerate over the next 12 months with the second generation of roads (ISR p. 2). The fullest account of bottlenecks and actions is the midterm review aide-memoire (mission 6 October - 21 November 2025, document dated 2025-11-21, disclosed 2026-05-07).

Bottlenecks (aide-memoire pp. 2-3): a US$90 million financing gap, including US$25 million to replenish the CERC, driven by the shift to people-centered design, heavier traffic loading needing stronger pavements, and inflation and design changes; a needed 18-month extension (paras. 5-6); unresolved application of the VAT exemption across both credits (para. 7); delays in Component 1 and procurement/contract management problems made worse by prolonged approvals and SDR/USD exchange losses; TANROADS' design-and-build bids for the Geita and Lindi second-generation roads came in about 70% and 64% above estimates and were cancelled for re-tendering (paras. 8, 13); delays on the six CERC contracts and occupational health and safety issues, which led to that component being downgraded (para. 10); slippage on the Iringa (Ipogolo)-Kilolo road (79% physical progress at 84% of contract time) due to the NMT lane, Ruaha Bridge girders, equipment stuck at Dar es Salaam port and the privately owned Ipogolo bus stand (para. 11); work-zone traffic management and road safety audit recommendations not implemented (para. 12).

Actions for the government side (implementing agencies), Table 1 (pp. 12-13): TARURA and TANROADS - meet the three AF effectiveness conditions (amendment letter, subsidiary agreements with the Ministry of Finance, revised Project Implementation Manual; by 30 Dec 2025 per para. 4), open designated accounts for IDA 77160, share annual work plans by 31 May each year, pay contractors and consultants on time, share names of deployed E&S officers; TARURA - confirm the VAT exemption interpretation in writing (by 30 Dec 2025 per para. 7), submit CBRM data for the 302 community groups and a CBRM replication proposal for 2026/27-2027/28, prioritize second-generation roads within available funds and sign the US$113.7 million second-generation road contracts within six months, revise the M&E framework and baselines for new indicators, resubmit the National District Roads Program ToR; TANROADS - submit the final Ipogolo bus stand design and flood control measures and the RSA compliance matrix, traffic management plan and revised work program (by 30 Nov 2025 per paras. 11-12), a design review and repackaging strategy for Geita and Lindi, rebid those two packages (US$30.8m and US$15.4m) within three months, a time-bound plan for high-value packages, have CERC contractors submit revised work plans, recruit an additional project accountant.

Actions involving the Bank: the World Bank team to run a technical mission to the CERC contracts in Lindi by early March 2026, followed by an implementation status mission (para. 59); joint items 'TARURA & World Bank' (agree and approve the road safety training concept note) and 'TRDS & WB' (confirm how the VAT exemption applies to both credits; the agreement on the approach to the CERC designated account sits next to it in the table, but the layout makes its responsible party ambiguous) (Table 1, p. 13). The Ministry of Finance is named for the subsidiary agreements and the VAT review (paras. 4, 7).
The table's date column is laid out separately from its rows in the document; deadlines are safest quoted where the paragraphs state them.
Later status: the September 2026 AF2 paper proposes US$25 million and the 18-month extension in response to the financing gap (AF2 paper pp. 1-4).

right_sources: Uses the latest ISR and the midterm review aide-memoire (40076267); the AF2 paper is optional.
grounded: Each bottleneck and action is cited to the aide-memoire paragraph or table; responsibilities match the table; no invented deadlines.
complete: Gives the main bottlenecks and separates actions assigned to the implementing agencies/government from those involving the Bank.
scoped: Says which documents and dates the answer reflects (an aide-memoire from November 2025 and an ISR from August 2026), and that later progress on the actions is not reported in them.

notes: A newer ISR or aide-memoire would change 'latest reporting'.
